translationRepairs: As governor-general of Huguang and concurrently commissioned to govern Hubei and Hunan, Xi Liang led troops from those provinces to escort the court into Shanxi and was at once appointed governor of the province.

Jointly commissioned by the Huguang governor-general and the governors of Hubei and Hunan, Xi Liang led troops from those provinces to escort the court into Shanxi and was at once appointed governor of the province.
以湖廣總督、湖北湖南巡撫會委 marks Xi Liang as jointly commissioned by those officeholders, not as Huguang governor-general himself; the proposed English corrects that agency error.

Xi Liang, as concurrently governor-general of Huguang and jointly commissioned governor of Hubei and Hunan, commanded Hubei and Hunan troops to enter for defense, received the imperial progress in Shanxi, and was immediately appointed governor.

Xi Liang, as jointly commissioned by the Huguang governor-general and the Hubei and Hunan governors, commanded Hubei and Hunan troops to enter for defense, received the imperial progress in Shanxi, and was immediately appointed governor.
Literal likewise misreads 會委 as Xi Liang holding those posts concurrently; he was commissioned by the Huguang governor-general and the Hubei and Hunan governors.
He was transferred to the post of Rehe governor-general.
He was transferred to the post of Rehe lieutenant-general.
熱河都統 is the Rehe banner dutong (lieutenant-general), not 總督; 'governor-general' is a real office-title error and the replacement is accurate.
He was transferred to be Rehe governor-general.
He was transferred to be Rehe lieutenant-general.
Literal repeats the same 都統/總督 conflation; Rehe lieutenant-general is the required rendering.

Xi Liang also, because the Two Eastern Provinces' neighbors divided occupation, [said that] without building a great trunk line one could not thread the veins and arteries; he therefore planned to build the railway from Jinzhou to Aihui.

Xi Liang also, because the Three Eastern Provinces' neighbors divided occupation, [said that] without building a great trunk line one could not thread the veins and arteries; he therefore planned to build the railway from Jinzhou to Aihui.
東三省 is the Three Eastern Provinces; 'Two' is a numeral error, and the proposed fix restores the correct count.
Xi Liang reflected that the two palaces had gone in fortune to Shaanxi: the peace settlement certainly had to be kept in view, yet defending Shanxi and guarding Shaanxi could not be neglected either.

Xi Liang reflected that the two palaces had made an imperial progress to Shaanxi: the peace settlement certainly had to be kept in view, yet defending Shanxi and guarding Shaanxi could not be neglected either.
幸陝 denotes the imperial progress (or flight) to Shaanxi; 'gone in fortune' is a false calque that obscures 幸, and 'imperial progress' restores the sense.
Enemies slandered him, however, and he was reassigned instead as Rehe governor-general, which he took up despite grave illness.
Enemies slandered him, however, and he was reassigned instead as Rehe Military Lieutenant-Governor (dutong), which he took up despite grave illness.
改授熱河都統 again names the Rehe dutong, not a governor-general; the proposed Military Lieutenant-Governor label matches the office.

When Korea first opened trade, Fu with American consul-general Shufeldt negotiated a draft commercial treaty to protect it, first calling Korea China's tributary state—solidly to guard against seizure—yet the Grand Council struck it out.

When Korea first opened trade, Fu with American commodore Shufeldt negotiated a draft commercial treaty to protect it, first calling Korea China's tributary state—solidly to guard against seizure—yet the Grand Council struck it out.
美提督 is a naval commodore/admiral title, not consul-general; the proposed office label is correct.

When Korea first opened to trade, Zhou Fu drafted a commercial treaty with American Minister Shufeldt that explicitly called Korea a Chinese dependency—a safeguard against foreign seizure—but the Grand Council struck that clause.

When Korea first opened to trade, Zhou Fu drafted a commercial treaty with American Commodore Shufeldt that explicitly called Korea a Chinese dependency—a safeguard against foreign seizure—but the Grand Council struck that clause.
Idiomatic 'Minister' likewise misrenders 美提督; Commodore correctly names Shufeldt's naval rank.
French troops had earlier reached Baoding, killed Acting Treasurer Ting Yong, and occupied the provincial yamen.
French troops had earlier reached Baoding, killed former Provincial Treasurer Ting Yong, and occupied the provincial yamen.
前布政使 means former provincial treasurer; 'Acting' invents a different status, and 'former' matches the Chinese.
He was soon promoted governor of Shandong but kept in Beijing to negotiate the Tianjin–Luanzhou railway question.
He was soon promoted governor of Shandong but ordered retained to negotiate the Tianjin–Luanzhou railway question.
詔留議津榆路事 says an edict ordered him retained to deliberate the railway matter; Beijing is not in the Chinese and should not be invented.
Yuanding said: 'Carefully uphold the national constitution.
Yuanding said: 'Carefully uphold the laws of the state.
國憲 here means the realm's laws or statutes, not a modern national constitution; the proposed wording matches the idiomatic sense and the Chinese.
Shortly he acted as provincial treasurer and protected the governorship.
Shortly he acted as provincial treasurer and served as acting governor.
護巡撫 is Qing acting tenure of the governorship; 'protected the governorship' is a false calque, and 'served as acting governor' is accurate.
Zhang traveled light to take office; when advisers urged an armed escort, he said: "That would provoke rebellion!"
Zhang took the convenient route to take office; when advisers urged an armed escort, he said: "That would provoke rebellion!"
便道之官 means taking office by a convenient route; 'traveled light' invents the sense of the next unit's 輕騎 and should be corrected.
Cengyang took a shortcut to office; some urged him to take troops along, saying: 'That would hasten rebellion!'
Cengyang took a shortcut to office; some urged him to take troops along. He said: 'That would hasten rebellion!'
After 或勸以兵從, 曰 marks Zhang Cengyang's reply, not the advisers' speech; the proposed reattribution is required.
The Yellow River ran more than a thousand li through Shandong; the channel had silted up while the dikes were thin, and annual breaches were a major disaster.
The river ran more than a thousand li through Shandong; the channel had silted up while the dikes were thin, and annual breaches were a major disaster.
The Chinese has only 河, not 黃河; adding 'Yellow' invents a specifier absent from the source, and the proposed 'the river' preserves fidelity.

Shixiang, moved with resolve to reform a century's abuses, memorialized: 'At the dynasty's founding, because of the Ming season's many added levies, popular livelihood was carved and exhausted—repeated edicts forbade cumulative exactions.

Shixiang, moved with resolve to reform a century's abuses, memorialized: 'At the dynasty's founding, because of the late Ming's many added levies, popular livelihood was carved and exhausted—repeated edicts forbade cumulative exactions.
明季 means the late Ming period; 'Ming season' is a false calque, and 'late Ming' is the standard sense.

Repeatedly he submitted memorials by proxy memorialization, requesting plans for self-strengthening, honoring the great foundation, and carrying out practical government—Emperor Dezong commended and accepted.

Repeatedly he submitted memorials for presentation, requesting plans for self-strengthening, honoring the great foundation, and carrying out practical government—Emperor Dezong commended and accepted.
疊上疏代奏 means repeatedly submitting memorials for presentation/transmission; 'by proxy memorialization' is unnatural and obscures 代奏.
After more than fifteen years he died at age eighty-five.
Fifteen years later he died at age eighty-five.
越十有五年 uses classical 有 as the numeral connector for fifteen years, not 'more than fifteen'; the proposed wording is exact.
